fields.description:
## Context (operator escalation R3/C11.3, 2026-08-12) — re-scoped 2026-08-11 after a premise audit

The code-review gate runs its Pass-2 verify judge (gates/code-review.yaml verify step). The
original filing claimed that 0 of ~1,400 recorded code_review_result_v2 sidecar findings carry a
`verification` block, and asked for the block to be persisted.

**That premise was disproven by a direct audit of the live store and item 1 is withdrawn.** Across
all 3,669 recorded REVIEW_RESULT events (1,377 code_review_result_v2 + 114 v1), 3,583 of 3,673
persisted code-review findings (97.5%) already carry `verification`, and every one of those blocks
holds exactly `{binary, severity_attributes}` — the shape item 1 proposed adding. Presence is
uniform over time (v1 2026-07: 358/358; v2 2026-07: 1592/1612; v2 2026-08: 1633/1703), so it is
not a recent fix. The analysis that produced the "0 findings" number read for the plan-review
field shape; code-review reaches the same result by a different mechanism —
`review_kernel.decide.pass3_over_findings` stamps `verification` onto every decided finding, and
`code_review.sidecar.build_payload`'s `_with_norm_ids` is a field-SPREAD (`{**f, "norm_id": ...}`)
that preserves every field, where plan-review's `_slim` is a field-SELECTION that must name
`verification` explicitly. There is no drop site, and the "no analog" claim was incorrect: the
analog is preservation rather than selection.

The 90 findings without a block are all legitimately unverified, not dropped: 53 are `tier="DET"`
(29 advisory, 24 blocking) plus 8 untiered — deterministic detector / fail-closed / bugfix-size-gate
findings that never enter Pass-2, so no verification exists to persist — and 29 are `tier="LLM"`,
`decision="indeterminate"`, `reason="no-verification"`, where Pass-2 emitted nothing for that index
and `pass3_decide` degraded them correctly.

What survives the audit is the operator's stated larger concern (R3): **nothing errors or warns when
an expected recording is absent.** `verification_recorded` appears nowhere in `src/`, `tests/`, or
`docs/`. That gap is real and is the whole of this ticket.

The original wording of the signal ("findings lack verification while verify ran") cannot be
implemented as written: it is true on any run carrying a DET-tier detector finding or an
indeterminate, i.e. routinely, so it would be a standing false alarm. The predicate is therefore
scoped to the findings that are actually expected to carry a block.

## Plan

1. In `_attach_code_review_metrics` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py) — which already computes
   `verify_requests`, the "did Pass-2 run" signal, into `coverage["metrics"]` — add a
   `verification_recorded` boolean to the same metrics dict.
2. Detection predicate (LLM-tier-scoped, so it can never become a standing false alarm): over the
   verdict's `blocking` + `advisory` + `dropped` + `indeterminate` buckets, a finding is EXPECTED to
   carry a block iff `tier == "LLM"` AND `decision != "indeterminate"` AND
   `reason != "no-verification"`. DET-tier and untiered findings are excluded (they never enter
   Pass-2). `verification_recorded` is False iff `verify_requests > 0` AND at least one expected
   finding has no truthy `verification`; True otherwise.
3. When the signal is False, log a WARNING naming the missing count out of the expected count, so
   the absence is both alertable (log) and measurable (metrics key).
4. Tests: signal cases in tests/unit/test_code_review_fp_ledger.py (the existing
   `_attach_code_review_metrics` home) — recorded-true on a healthy verdict, recorded-false with a
   warning when an expected block is missing, and recorded-true when the ONLY blockless findings are
   DET-tier / indeterminate (the false-alarm guard). Plus a regression pin in
   tests/unit/test_code_review_ws4.py asserting the sidecar payload round-trips a finding's
   `{binary, severity_attributes}` through `build_payload` — pinning today's already-correct
   behaviour so the field-spread cannot silently regress to a field-selection.

Advisory only: this touches `coverage["metrics"]` and never `verdict["verdict"]`. Sidecar readers
are schema-tolerant, so a new metrics key is additive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `coverage["metrics"]["verification_recorded"]` is present on every finalized code-review
      verdict, and is False with a WARNING naming the missing count when Pass-2 ran but an
      LLM-tier decided finding carries no verification block. Verify:
      `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_fp_ledger.py -q`
- [x] The signal does NOT fire when the only blockless findings are DET-tier or
      `decision="indeterminate"` / `reason="no-verification"` — the standing-false-alarm guard.
      Verify: covered by a dedicated test in the same module.
- [x] A sidecar payload round-trips a verified finding's `verification.binary` and
      `verification.severity_attributes` through `build_payload`. Verify:
      `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k "code_review or sidecar"`
- [x] Existing sidecar readers are unaffected (additive metrics key only). Verify:
      `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k "sidecar"`
